title: Terminated Dinosaur Era
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

Terminated Dinosaur Era

A A The age of dinosaurs, which ended with the cataclysmic bang of a meteor impact 65 million years ago, may also have begun with one. Recently, researchers have found the first direct, although tentative, geological evidence of a meteor impact occurring 200 million years ago. This appears to coincide with the extinction of half the major species of life, yet at the same time paving the way for the age of the dinosaurs, which was then a small group.

B B The reason why and when dinosaurs appeared on earth has been widely discussed. As no specific research has been done on the first appearance of dinosaurs and their rise to dominance, it is impossible to make any specific conclusions. However, when studying the chemical composition of the earth's rocks and minerals, there does appear to be signs of a major occurrence, likely a meteor impact, just before the rise of the familiar dinosaur communities started appearing, says Dr. Paul E. Olsen, who is a professor of earth and environmental sciences in Columbia University's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory in Palisades, NY.

C C Vertebrate fossils from 80 sites in four different ancient rift basins—a group of rifts that were created when North America separated from the supercontinent around 190-230 million years ago—were collected and studied. Within the layer of rock which corresponded to the time of the extinction, an elevated amount of iridium, which is a rare element, was found. Part of the platinum group of elements, iridium is a precious metal and is found more often in meteorites than in rocks.

D D A similar discovery of iridium in the 1970s in rocks which are 65 million-year-old led to the theory that a meteor caused the extinction on the dinosaurs. Until further evidence was found, and the impact site of the meteor was discovered off the Yucatan Peninsula, this theory remained controversial. This new discovery of iridium would need to be examined similarly, as the amount of iridium found in this latest discovery was only one-tenth of the iridium found in the earlier discovery. This may mean that this meteor contained less iridium or was smaller than the other meteor. Or it may not have come from a meteor at all, because iridium can also come from inside the earth, such as in a volcanic explosion. According to Dr. Michael J. Benton, a professor of vertebrate paleontology, this event is a reasonably convincing evidence of an iridium spike.

E E In a database containing 10000 fossilized footprints found in former lake basins ranging from Virginia to Nova Scotia, scientists found more evidence of rapid extinction. Footprints can provide a good picture of the various types of animals walking around. Although individual species of animals cannot be usually identified, just like the footprints of a house cat look similar to the footprints of a baby tiger, they are more plentiful than fossil bones. Given that sediment piles up rapidly in lake basins, the researchers were able to date each footprint based on the layer of rock where it was found. Dr. Olsen said that because of this, it is easy to see signs of massive fauna change. As a result, they determined that there was a sudden change 200 million years ago to the fauna walking across what is now the East Coast of North America.

F F The tracks of several major reptile groups continue almost up to the layer of rock marking the end of the Triassic geologic period 202 million years ago, and then vanish in younger layers from the Jurassic Period. ‘I think the footprint methodology is very novel and very exciting,’ said Dr. Peter D. Ward, a professor of geology at the University of Washington. He called the data ‘requiring more research’. Last year, researchers led by Dr. Ward reported that the types of carbon in rock changed abruptly at this time, indicating a sudden dying off of plants over less than 50000 years. The footprint research reinforces the hypothesis that the extinction was sudden.

G G Several groups of dinosaurs survived that extinction, and the footprints show that new groups emerged soon afterward. Before the extinction, about one-fifth of the footprints were left by dinosaurs; after the extinction, more than half were from dinosaurs. The changes, the researchers said, occurred within 30000 years—a geological blink of an eye. The scientists postulate that the asteroid or comet impact and the resulting death of Triassic competitors allowed a few groups of carnivorous dinosaurs to evolve in size very quickly and dominate the top of the terrestrial food chain globally.

H H Among the creatures that disappeared in the extinction were the dominant predators at the time: 15-foot-long rauisuchians with great knife-like teeth and phytosaurs that resembled large crocodiles. ‘Dinosaurs first evolved about 230 million years ago, but they were small, competing in a crowded ecological niche. Before the extinction 200 million years ago, the largest of the meat-eating dinosaurs were about the size of large dogs. Not terribly impressive.’ Dr. Olsen said. The dinosaurs quickly grew. The toe-to-heel length of the foot of a meat eater from the Jurassic period was on average 20 percent longer than its Triassic ancestor. Larger feet can carry bigger bodies; the scientists infer the dinosaurs doubled in weight, eventually evolving into fearsome velociraptors, Tyrannosaurus rex and other large carnivorous dinosaurs.

I I The spurt in evolution is similar to the rise of mammals after the extinction of dinosaurs. Mammals, no larger than small dogs during the age of dinosaurs, diversified into tigers, elephants, whales and people after the reptilian competition died away. The success of the dinosaurs after the Triassic-Jurassic extinction may be why they did not survive the second extinction. ‘Small animals always do better in catastrophic situations,’ Dr. Olsen said, ‘because they can survive on smaller amounts of food.’ He also pointed out that scientists now believe the small dinosaurs did survive. ‘We just call them birds.’ he said. Modern birds descended from a group of two-legged dinosaurs known as theropods, whose members include the towering Tyrannosaurus rex and the smaller velociraptors. The theropods most closely related to avians generally weighed between 100 and 500 pounds — giants compared to most modern birds — and they had large snouts, big teeth, and not much between the ears. A velociraptor, for example, had a skull like a coyote's and a brain roughly the size of a pigeon's.

J J For decades, paleontologists' only fossil link between birds and dinosaurs was archaeopteryx, a hybrid creature with feathered wings but with the teeth and long bony tail of a dinosaur. These animals appeared to have acquired their birdlike features — feathers, wings and flight — in just 10 million years, a mere flash in evolutionary time.

Questions 1–6

Use the information in the passage to match the people (listed A-C) with opinions or deeds (listed 1-6) below.

NB You may use any letters more than once.

1 During disasters, large animals are at a position of disadvantage

2 Profound variations in carbon types indicate massive extinction of vegetation

3 Adding footprint investigation makes the identification of changes in earth's animal species less difficult

4 A meteor impact before dinosaurs' appearance is suggested by geochemical evidence

5 Footprint study is a new research method

6 A compelling evidence of an iridium spike was found

A Paul Olsen
B Michael Benton
C Peter Ward

Questions 7–13

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

Choose

TRUEif the statement agrees with the information
FALSEif the statement contradicts the information
NOT GIVENif there is no information on this

7 The rare element, iridium, was presented both on earth and in meteorites.

8 The meteor impact theory had been suspected before the discovery of the impact site and other supporting evidence.

9 Footprints can provide very limited information in comparison to fossil bones.

10 According to scientists, the transition to a dinosaur-dominated era took place very qui-ckly by geological time scale.

11 The creatures that disappeared in extinction were the dominant 15-foot-long rauisu-chians and large crocodiles.

12 Tyrannosaurus rex was larger in body size than other carnivorous dinosaurs.

13 Large dinosaurs did worse in catastrophes because it was hard to find shelter.
